## Purpose
The frontend's pipeline-run state manager: it launches runs over REST (`POST /api/runs` via `RunConnectionProvider`), and reduces the stream of incoming SSE pipeline events (`pipeline_start`, `agent_start/chunk/complete/error`, `task_progress`, `pipeline_complete/failed/cancelled`, etc.) into a single `PipelineRunState` the run screen renders from.

## Shape
- `useWorkflow()` â€” the exported hook; owns `pipelineState` and exposes `startPipeline`, `resetPipeline`, `handleMessage`, `submitQuestionnaire`, `retainClarifyRound`, `retainAgentEdit`, `reconcileTerminalStatus`.
- `handlePipelineMessage` â€” the standalone, transport-agnostic reducer (exported so the parent's SSE handler and tests can drive it directly) that switches over `msg.type` and applies each case to `PipelineRunState`.
- `ACCUMULATING_FRAME_TYPES` / `isRedelivery` / `markApplied` â€” a redelivery guard wrapping every accumulating event type (chunk/thinking/tool_call/hook_run/validator_result) so a durable replay (REST + SSE both delivering the same event) never double-applies it.
- `TERMINAL_MARKER_BY_STATUS` / `terminalMarkers` / `applyTerminalStatus` â€” the single definition of what a terminal run status (`completed`/`cancelled`/`failed`/`degraded`) does to run state, reused by the `pipeline_complete`/`pipeline_failed`/`pipeline_cancelled` cases and by `reconcileTerminalStatus`.
- `deriveSpecRevisionCount` â€” derives which spec-revision cycle a run is in from how many times the pipeline's first step has (re)started, scoped positionally rather than to any named agent/workflow.
- `frameIdentity` â€” the durable identity of one event frame (`event_id` â†’ `seq` â†’ an unstamped positional fallback), used by the redelivery guard.

## Why this shape
The reducer consolidates several previously-duplicated concerns (documented inline as ISS-082, ISS-126, ISS-063) into single definitions â€” one redelivery gate instead of per-field dedup checks, and one terminal-status vocabulary instead of three open-coded call sites â€” specifically because a durable run can be replayed over two transports (REST then SSE) and a naive reducer would double-count or desync state across reconnects/resumes.
